blocks.text: Velthusen (Beytrag zur Aufklär. des Dankliedes Hiskiae, in den Beyträgen zur Beförderung theologischer Kenntnisse, edited by J. A. Cramer, vol. 1, p. 60. 61. note) thinks that this difference in spelling arose because the ancient Hebrews lacked any fixed sign by which to express the sound mixed from u and i (ü), which is heard in Ssüs, סוס, and so used now the letter י, now ו.
Linn. Syst. vol. 1, part 2, p. 1019, 13th ed.

But because the swallow is called by the name סוס neither in the Arabic dialect nor in the Syriac, Paulus, in his Clavis in Iesaj., p. 216, denies that this word was used by the Hebrews to signify the swallow, and holds that it was used only of the horse. As if there were not many words peculiar to only one dialect or another! Cf. Velthusen on the Song of Hezekiah in the Symbolae Kilonienses, vol. 2, p. 325, note 51. Moreover, by what right the horse should be counted among the migratory birds in Ierem. VIII, 7., I can scarcely understand.
See Athenaeus, book 8, ch. 15, and Eustathius on the Odyssey, φ' [phi].
